key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current distinctly influence molten pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide welding process optimization for low-expansion Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics
Evaluation of laser power, welding speed, and welding current
evidence_signal: Across 5–6 kW, 0.5–0.8 m/min, and 150–170 A, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size, higher speed reduced penetration and weld width, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract reports trends within limited parameter ranges but provides no quantitative simulation-validation errors or mechanical performance results.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
